vision_report.narrative_description: The Mexican Mint seedling in the black pot demonstrates remarkable stability and health throughout the observation period, with its turgid, light green leaves showing no signs of stress. The soil consistently appears moist, supporting its vigor. In stark contrast, the Money Plant cutting in the white cup exhibits a clear and progressive decline in health. Starting with a subtle droop, its single prominent leaf becomes significantly curled and slumped by T-1, a state that persists into the CURRENT image. While the leaf retains its green hue, its dullness and posture are indicative of moderate to severe stress, likely stemming from challenges in water absorption or nutrient deficiency inherent to its water propagation environment. No other incidental growths or biome-wide anomalies were detected, apart from a noticeable shift in overall scene brightness from T-2 onwards.
